---
title: "Same Every Time"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Three Kinds of Machine. **Objective:** decide whether an LLM belongs inside a pipeline, and keep the pipeline reproducible if it does.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim.</span>
:::

A pipeline earns trust by giving the same answer from the same input. An LLM call can return different text from run to run, so putting one inside a step changes what the pipeline is.

**Prefer to keep the LLM out of the run.** Use it to *write* a script, then test the script and run the script. The script is deterministic and reviewable.

If an LLM call really must be a step (tidying messy free-text labels, say), contain it:

- **Record** the model name and version, and the exact prompt, with the outputs. This is necessary but not sufficient: even a pinned model may not return identical text every time.
- **Cache** results keyed by input (saved outputs; a different sense from the prompt cache used in Claude Code sessions), so a re-run does not change them silently.
- **Validate** each output against a fixed set (a species list, a schema) and fail loudly when it does not match.
- **Keep a human-check sample**: look at a random handful every time.
- **Keep it away from data you may not send out.** See The Locked Cabinet.
